all_consequential_claim_checks.candidate_exact_text: Use valid-sample majority when an output cell should represent the dominant class; use nearest when it should copy one representative source sample. Never interpolate class codes numerically.
all_consequential_claim_checks.reasoning: Categorical IDs encode membership rather than an arithmetic magnitude. Majority gives the dominant valid label only for the selected footprint/contributor policy; nearest chooses one sample. This is a conditional categorical-product recommendation, not a promise that built-in mode propagates an external mask.

all_consequential_claim_checks.candidate_exact_text: Conditional recommendation: majority for area-oriented products; nearest for sample-preserving or compatibility products.
all_consequential_claim_checks.reasoning: Dominant-class and representative-sample objectives justify different alternatives. Area-oriented here means a dominant class over a footprint, not exact class-area conservation; no universal default is imposed.

all_consequential_claim_checks.candidate_exact_text: Rasterio says no resampling method is universally correct. Its 1.3.10 enum defines mode as the most frequent sampled value. The categorical policy here is a product recommendation, not a source guarantee.
all_consequential_claim_checks.reasoning: The no-universal-method statement and released mode definition are present. The candidate explicitly separates its categorical policy from source guarantees. The resampling locator is imperfect; the supporting universal-method sentence itself is inside its range.

all_consequential_claim_checks.candidate_exact_text: Assumes categorical labels and defined target footprints; specify contributors and weights for reprojection or unequal footprints.
all_consequential_claim_checks.reasoning: Footprints/contributors must be chosen before a reducer has meaning. Equal sample counts do not necessarily represent equal area after unequal footprints or reprojection; specifying weights is the appropriate open condition.

all_consequential_claim_checks.candidate_exact_text: Count only valid labels. Define ties, minimum valid coverage, and empty output. If built-in mode does not meet the mask/tie policy, use explicit counts.
all_consequential_claim_checks.reasoning: Restricting counts to valid labels preserves mask semantics. Tie, coverage and empty-cell choices are not selected by the mapped sources. An explicit reducer is a reasonable fallback; built-in mode is not asserted to satisfy these policies.

all_consequential_claim_checks.candidate_exact_text: Nearest copies one sample; grid alignment can omit small classes.
all_consequential_claim_checks.reasoning: Nearest selects one sample. A footprint containing a minority class can select another class at its sampling location, so grid alignment can omit that minority. This is a geometric consequence, not a documentation guarantee about minority-class survival.

all_consequential_claim_checks.candidate_exact_text: Dominant valid label per footprint; needs tie, coverage, and empty-cell rules.
all_consequential_claim_checks.reasoning: The majority alternative is defined by valid contributing labels, with ties/coverage/empty output left explicit. It remains distinct from the released mode function until runtime mask and tie behavior are checked.

all_consequential_claim_checks.candidate_exact_text: One source label and its validity; simple, but not a footprint summary.
all_consequential_claim_checks.reasoning: The alternative carries the chosen source label with validity evaluated under the selected mask. It is not represented as estimating all labels in a footprint. Reading/resampling data alone is not claimed to implement the separate validity policy.

all_consequential_claim_checks.candidate_exact_text: Choose by intended output meaning; neither method is universal.
all_consequential_claim_checks.reasoning: Selection by intended output meaning is supported by the brief and absence of a universally correct method. No required alternative is unjustifiably rejected.

all_consequential_claim_checks.candidate_exact_text: Proposed: test unequal and tied counts, a small class, partial validity, and an empty footprint; outputs must be source labels or declared invalid.
all_consequential_claim_checks.reasoning: Unequal counts, ties, minority class, partial and empty validity test distinct failure modes. The label-or-invalid invariant detects numerical interpolation of categorical codes. These are proposals without claimed passing results.

all_consequential_claim_checks.candidate_exact_text: Sources do not specify mode tie-breaking or its mask propagation for this policy; test the pinned runtime or use an explicit reducer.

The claim is read as a limit of these sources, not absence of public implementation knowledge. Checking the pinned runtime or choosing explicit counts retains useful paths.

all_consequential_claim_checks.reasoning: Band validity and dataset validity have different scope/precedence; an application inclusion/quality mask has no role fixed by the brief. Keeping them distinct prevents treating a class code as a mask.

all_consequential_claim_checks.candidate_exact_text: Start with selected-band validity; document whether a separate mask restricts or replaces it.
all_consequential_claim_checks.reasoning: Selected-band validity is a sensible starting policy for a class-band task. Separate masks may restrict or authoritatively replace it only under a declared input contract; the candidate does not prescribe universal AND.

all_consequential_claim_checks.candidate_exact_text: Rasterio uses nonzero GDAL mask bytes for valid and NumPy masked-array True for invalid. A .msk can supersede nodata. dataset_mask may use the OR of band masks when nodata is its fallback.
all_consequential_claim_checks.reasoning: Each component checks: nonzero GDAL validity, inverse NumPy polarity, .msk precedence over nodata, and band-mask OR only in dataset_mask nodata fallback after higher-priority masks.

all_consequential_claim_checks.candidate_exact_text: Use read_masks(class_band) != 0, or invert read(masked=True).mask. Do not assume dataset_mask means selected-band validity.
all_consequential_claim_checks.reasoning: The preferred read_masks(class_band) != 0 path is correct. The alternative raw inversion of read(masked=True).mask is not guaranteed to yield a cell-shaped array: Rasterio 1.3.10 explicitly supplies np.ma.nomask on the all_valid path, and NumPy documents its scalar form. The candidate never requires expanding this representation before the valid_count = count(mask != 0) calculation. In an all-valid 2x2 analytical example, counting the inverted scalar counts one value rather than four cells. Even selecting the band explicitly does not remove the scalar-mask edge case. Use the preferred mask-read path, or normalize a selected-band masked read with getmaskarray/broadcast-to-shape first. This is a source-derived counterexample, not an executed raster test.

all_consequential_claim_checks.candidate_exact_text: GDAL defines the affine transform coefficients. Their pixel and line basis vectors imply coordinate-plane cell area abs(GT1*GT5 - GT2*GT4); this determinant is a mathematical derivation, not an area formula stated by the source.
all_consequential_claim_checks.reasoning: From X=GT0+i*GT1+j*GT2 and Y=GT3+i*GT4+j*GT5, the unit-cell basis is u=(GT1,GT4), v=(GT2,GT5). The parallelogram magnitude is |det(u,v)|=|GT1*GT5-GT2*GT4|. The candidate explicitly labels this as a derivation, not a GDAL area formula.

all_consequential_claim_checks.candidate_exact_text: valid_count = count(mask != 0). For a constant affine grid, multiply by abs(GT1*GT5 - GT2*GT4); north-up simplifies to abs(GT1*GT5).
all_consequential_claim_checks.reasoning: Nonzero-mask cell count times the constant affine determinant is coordinate-plane area. North-up zero rotation removes the cross term. The formula uses the mask corresponding to the chosen grid; it is not a physical-area claim for arbitrary CRS. However, the offered raw .mask-inversion alternative can supply scalar nomask rather than that cell-shaped grid. D04 is the missing construction condition that can corrupt this otherwise correct count and area formula.

B01.stated_source_fact: The task selects Rasterio 1.3.10, categorical downsampling and validity summaries, two bounded alternatives, optional continuous-band investigation, and proposed validation. Product mask roles, thresholds, grid and area units are not selected.

M01.stated_source_fact: GDAL valid-data masks use unsigned bytes with nonzero validity. NumPy masked-array True indicates invalidity.

M02.stated_source_fact: Every band has a mask; read_masks(1) reads the first band mask as a two-dimensional uint8 array.

M03.stated_source_fact: Valid values rounded to zero can collide with an eight-bit nodata sentinel; a repaired authoritative mask can mark some zero-valued pixels valid.

M04.stated_source_fact: Writing a validity mask need not alter data or nodata metadata. An existing .msk sidecar supplies masks instead of the nodata metadata.

M05.stated_source_fact: The selected-band masked read has opposite mask polarity; the documented identity compares inversion of read(N, masked=True).mask with read_masks(N).

M06.stated_source_fact: Dataset validity has precedence: .msk/dataset alpha/internal mask; shadow-nodata RGBA band 4; then nodata-based OR of band masks; otherwise all valid. It applies per dataset rather than per band.

M07.stated_source_fact: The example combines band masks and chooses a sieve size empirically; representations depend on format/configuration. This example is not an application mask contract.

R01.stated_source_fact: Resampling changes the raster grid and values, including changes during reprojection; a changed output shape is accompanied by a scaled image transform in the example.

R02.stated_source_fact: The resampling guidance rejects one generally correct method and points to the Resampling enum for available methods.

R03.stated_source_fact: Nearest is the documented default and may not suit continuous data; bilinear/cubic can suit those data and average can help retain chosen numerical properties.

E01.stated_source_fact: The released enum describes nearest-neighbor sampling, weighted averaging of non-nodata contributors, and mode selection of the most frequent sampled value. Values are nearest=0, average=5, mode=6.

E02.stated_source_fact: The named nearest/bilinear/cubic/average/mode methods are documented as available with GDAL >=1.10. The enum does not specify this product mask policy or a mode tie rule.

W01.stated_source_fact: Windows select rectangular subsets and permit work on data exceeding RAM; offsets and dimensions are expressed in pixels.

W02.stated_source_fact: A small read can require complete storage chunks; an unchunked dataset can require reading the entire dataset even for a one-pixel requested window.

W03.stated_source_fact: Windows matching blocks improve read/write efficiency; block_shapes and block_windows expose layout. GDAL permits bands with differing block layouts.

G01.stated_source_fact: The affine transform maps pixel/line coordinates to projected or geographic coordinates with six coefficients; its pixel and line basis vectors are (GT1,GT4) and (GT2,GT5).

G02.stated_source_fact: A north-up transform has zero GT2 and GT4; GT1 and GT5 specify pixel dimensions, with negative GT5 for north-up as noted earlier.

I01.stated_source_fact: Rasterio 1.3.10 masked reads use np.ma.nomask when all band mask flags are all_valid, otherwise constructing a shaped mask array. An integer selected-band index yields two dimensions; an omitted index selects all bands.

I02.stated_source_fact: The released mask-read API returns a two-dimensional selected-band uint8 mask. Its dataset-mask implementation uses dataset-wide mask selection or reduction of band masks.

N01.primary_locator: getmaskarray definition and Result when mask == nomask example, normalized page lines 247–249 and 284–295; generic mask guide note at normalized line 174
N01.stated_source_fact: A fully valid masked array can have scalar nomask rather than a Boolean array. getmaskarray supplies an all-False mask array matching the data shape for that case.

P01.stated_source_fact: The metadata identifies release 1.3.10 and lists numpy without a version pin. The brief likewise provides no NumPy runtime version.

defects.source_facts: The selected release explicitly constructs masked reads with np.ma.nomask on its all_valid branch. The NumPy 1.26 manual distinguishes this scalar from a shape-matched Boolean mask and documents getmaskarray normalization. The release metadata and original brief do not select a NumPy version.
defects.reviewer_inference: An allowed all-valid 2x2 selected band can produce a scalar no-mask value. Inverting that scalar and counting its nonzero entries yields one value, not four valid source cells; affine count-to-area inherits the error. This is an analytical counterexample, not an observed raster execution.
defects.materiality: The expressly offered alternative can silently corrupt the task’s core valid-cell/valid-area summary. Correct polarity is insufficient without matching cell shape. The default read_masks(class_band) path is unaffected; the defect does not invalidate the conditional majority-versus-nearest decision.
defects.required_condition: Use the existing selected-band read_masks array path, or obtain the selected-band masked data and invert np.ma.getmaskarray(data) (or explicitly expand nomask to the band grid) before counting/indexing; preserve the selected band and two-dimensional grid.
defects.validation_proposal: Add an all-valid, no-nodata 2x2 selected-band case and a multiband case; assert a cell-shaped Boolean validity mask and count four for the first case. Proposal only; no execution.
defects.runtime_limit: No installed NumPy/GDAL combination or input raster was supplied or inspected. The failure condition follows the pinned Rasterio branch and versioned NumPy documented API; no result on a particular machine is asserted.

defects.title: Resampling source line range excludes the continuous-data guidance
defects.source_facts: The section starts at raw line 53. The continuous-data nearest/bilinear/cubic/average guidance is at 62–68, outside the claimed range. The no-general-correct-method sentence at 56–57 is inside it.
defects.materiality: This reduces precise citation usability, particularly for the optional lead. The correctly bound, complete 68-line source and named section retain all support; no scientific recommendation changes.
defects.correction: Use 53–68 for the section, or 56–60 and 62–68 for the separate claims.

defects.title: Mask locators miss valid-zero ambiguity and masked-array inversion
defects.source_facts: Lines 30–43 show opening the sample and nodata metadata; the valid-zero collision discussion is 85–92. Inverse NumPy polarity is 12–15 and the selected-band mask identity is 203–216.
defects.materiality: The source itself and its identity are correct, and all meaning is preserved, but the precision claims are wrong. This locator defect is distinct from D04’s released scalar-mask condition.

defects.title: Window read-caveat locator points to a write example
defects.source_facts: Beyond-RAM motivation is 6–8; the complete-chunk/unchunked-file read caveat is 57–66. Lines 72–84 are the write example, not the caveat. Block differences are correctly reachable in the supplied later range.
